hero.line2: I'm an M.F.A. candidate at Jiangnan University studying how people interpret, trust, and rely on emerging AI and immersive systems in situated contexts. I build interactive prototypes, conduct mixed-methods user studies, and translate empirical findings into design implications for accessibility, AI-mediated communication, and cultural interaction.

paragraphs: My research asks how people experience, interpret, and evaluate the technologies we build. I combine interactive prototypes — Unity AR apps, TouchDesigner installations, Figma interfaces — with surveys, interviews, and structural equation models. My M.F.A. thesis research examines how augmented reality can support cultural heritage experiences in museum spaces, using SOR theory, TAM, and flow models to understand visitor engagement (N=388, CB-SEM).

I am developing a PRISMA-based systematic review on generative AI for accessibility, screening 3,570 papers and qualitatively coding 136 of them to map how the field is, and is not, serving people with disabilities. I've published across venues including Heritage, SAGE Open, Applied Sciences, and Scientific Reports — six papers so far, with more in the pipeline.

I came to research through design. My B.F.A. in visual communication taught me to care about how things look and feel; my M.F.A. taught me to care about whether they actually work. These days I split my time between making things and measuring their impact — a combination I'd like to keep pursuing in a PhD. Outside of work: I design typefaces, take too many photos, and have strong opinions about museum exhibition design.
about.highlight: I'm currently looking for a summer 2026 research internship — especially projects in human-AI interaction, accessibility, AI-mediated communication, learning, or immersive cultural interaction. If your lab could use a researcher who can prototype and run rigorous user studies, I'd love to chat.

projects.title: REMEMBERY
projects.subtitle: Multi-Stakeholder Alzheimer's Care App
projects.cardBlurb: UX design across four user groups — patients, family caregivers, doctors, and social workers. Accessibility-first approach to cognitive decline and care coordination.
projects.description: A mobile application co-designed for four user groups within the Alzheimer's care ecosystem: patients managing cognitive decline, family caregivers coordinating daily support, doctors tracking clinical progress, and social workers allocating community resources. The design process began with stakeholder interviews and persona development to map the distinct needs of each group. For patients, the interface prioritizes simplified navigation, high-contrast visuals, and cognitive training exercises. For caregivers, it surfaces emergency workflows and care coordination tools. For clinicians, it provides a monitoring dashboard. For social workers, it supports case management and resource matching. Accessibility was not retrofitted — WCAG guidelines informed every wireframe from the start, shaping decisions about font sizing, touch targets, color contrast, and navigation hierarchy. The project demonstrates a complete user-centered design process from needs assessment through iterative prototyping to high-fidelity interactive mockups.
projects.tools: Figma · Stakeholder Interviews · Persona Development · Iterative Prototyping · WCAG Accessibility Guidelines

projects.title: NUA Museum
projects.subtitle: Website UX Redesign for University Museum
projects.cardBlurb: Heuristic evaluation + task analysis + IA redesign for Nanjing University of the Arts museum website. Structured around visitor goals.
projects.description: A comprehensive UX redesign for the Nanjing University of the Arts museum website. The project began with a heuristic evaluation identifying pain points in content discovery, navigation clarity, and visual hierarchy. Visitor task analysis — based on observing how students, faculty, and external visitors used the site — revealed that key functions like exhibition browsing, event registration, and collection exploration were buried under unclear navigation paths. The redesigned information architecture restructured content around three primary visitor goals. A visual refresh updated typography, color palette, and spacing while maintaining the institution's brand identity. The project demonstrates applied UX methodology in a real-world cultural institution context: from diagnostic evaluation through structural redesign to visual implementation.
projects.tools: Figma · Heuristic Evaluation · Task Analysis · Information Architecture · Visual Design

projects.title: 木上生画
projects.subtitle: Gamified Cultural Heritage EdTech App
projects.cardBlurb: iPad app for exploring traditional woodblock print heritage. Full UX process from card-sorting to high-fidelity interactive prototype.
projects.description: An iPad application designed to teach the centuries-old craft of Zhuxianzhen woodblock printing through interactive, gamified learning. The UX process followed a structured methodology: card-sorting exercises to define the information architecture, low-fidelity wireframes for rapid concept validation, and high-fidelity interactive prototypes built in Adobe XD. The app organizes content across three learning modules: History Tracing explores the origins and evolution of woodblock printing across Chinese dynasties; Craft Techniques demonstrates the step-by-step production process through interactive animations; and Proverb Games transforms traditional folk sayings into playful matching and puzzle challenges. The project demonstrates how structured UX research methods — from information architecture to prototyping — can transform passive cultural consumption into active, self-directed discovery.

projects.title: TEXTILE 2050
projects.subtitle: Interactive Installation with Physical Computing
projects.cardBlurb: Arduino + TouchDesigner installation exploring sustainable futures. Exhibited at university gallery — visitors physically engage with textile-inspired interfaces.
projects.description: A future-sustainability themed interactive installation that invites visitors to physically engage with textile-inspired interfaces. Arduino pressure sensors and ultrasonic distance sensors detect touch and proximity, triggering real-time generative visuals through TouchDesigner. A speculative future factory environment — modeled in Blender — serves as the visual canvas. Visitors press fabric swatches to grow virtual plants or approach sensors to reveal hidden narrative layers about sustainable textile production. The installation was publicly exhibited at the university gallery. The project demonstrates end-to-end prototyping capability: hardware sensor integration, real-time graphics programming, 3D environmental modeling, and exhibition deployment. It explores a core HCI question: can embodied, tangible interaction communicate abstract environmental futures more effectively than passive media?

projects.title: LISTEN
projects.subtitle: Multimodal Sensory Interaction Concept
projects.cardBlurb: Interactive installation concept exploring auditory-visual synesthesia. TouchDesigner real-time graphics driven by spatial audio input.
projects.description: An interactive installation concept that explores auditory-visual synesthesia — the perceptual crossing of sound and sight. Using TouchDesigner for real-time generative graphics synchronized with a spatial audio system, the installation creates an immersive environment where visual forms — colors, patterns, and movements — respond dynamically to sonic input. A 3D environment modeled in Blender serves as the spatial canvas for this cross-modal experience. The concept investigates how feedback across sensory channels shapes perception and emotional response: when hearing and seeing intertwine, what new dimensions of experience emerge? The project contributes to research on multisensory interaction design by demonstrating how creative coding and spatial design can be composed into a unified, perception-driven experience.

projects.title: 会意AD
projects.subtitle: Immersive Health Communication Space
projects.cardBlurb: Immersive spatial experience communicating Alzheimer's awareness. Environmental storytelling translates medical concepts into embodied experience.
projects.description: An immersive spatial experience designed to communicate Alzheimer's disease awareness to the general public. The installation uses environmental storytelling — spatial design, curated lighting, soundscapes, and information graphics — to translate complex neurological concepts into an embodied, emotionally resonant visitor experience. Visitors move through spaces that simulate memory fragmentation, temporal disorientation, and sensory overload, using metaphor and sensory immersion to make invisible cognitive conditions tangibly felt. The project demonstrates how human-centered spatial design can bridge the gap between clinical knowledge and public understanding, turning abstract medical information into experiential knowledge.

projects.title: 敦煌奇妙夜
projects.subtitle: Immersive Interactive Installation with Physical Computing
projects.cardBlurb: Flashlight-driven immersive installation exploring Dunhuang murals. TouchDesigner + real-time 3D animation triggered by visitor interaction.
projects.description: An immersive interactive installation that brings the ancient murals of Dunhuang Mogao Cave 220 to life. Visitors enter a dimly lit cave-like space and use a custom flashlight to explore: when the light beam touches specific figures in the mural, those characters awaken as real-time 3D animations accompanied by traditional Chinese music. The installation was built with TouchDesigner for projection mapping and webcam-based light tracking, Blender for 3D character modeling, and AIGC tools for generating reference imagery. Multiple visitors can interact simultaneously, with different light-triggered regions activating different animations. The physical space was constructed from cardboard, foam, and paint to recreate the texture and atmosphere of the original cave. The project explores how tangible interaction, spatial storytelling, and real-time media can make cultural heritage feel alive and participatory.
projects.tools: TouchDesigner · Blender · Projection Mapping · Webcam Tracking · AIGC · Physical Construction
